http://www.bgnes.com/society/poland-deta.text: Polish authorities have detained a Russian national accused of planning to kill a dual Ukrainian-US citizen in Warsaw on Moscow’s orders, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said. Tusk told reporters that the suspect was arrested on Friday, August 7. “This is the first case of its kind in which someone acting on Russian orders decided to carry out an attack against a US citizen on the territory of another NATO country,” the Polish prime minister said. According to Tusk, officers from Poland’s Internal Security Agency (ABW) and the police arrested the suspect in cooperation with US services. “We have to assume that Putin’s regime will try to eliminate people who, for various reasons, are considered inconvenient,” Tusk said. He added that Warsaw would “probably face similar pressure again.” Poland, a member of both NATO and the European Union on the alliance’s eastern flank, has repeatedly accused Russia of sabotage since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. In June, Russian cartoonist and Putin critic Semyon Skrepetsky, whose real name was Robert Kuzovkov, was shot dead in eastern Poland. Tusk later described the killing as a “political assassination.” Several opponents of the Russian authorities have been targeted in attacks abroad, including in the United Kingdom, Germany and Lithuania, AFP noted. Moscow has consistently denied involvement in such attacks. | BGNES
